project_overview.purpose: A Spring Boot REST API service built on Java 17 that models a DVD rental store using the Sakila database, providing comprehensive CRUD operations, relationship management, and complex querying capabilities via QueryDSL and Blaze-Persistence.
functionality: Expose REST endpoints for managing actors, films, customers, rentals, staff, stores, addresses, cities, and payment transactions.
Authenticate users via Spring Security and JWT token generation.
Transform domain entities and DTOs into HATEOAS-compliant hypermedia response models.
Execute complex pagination, filtering, and text searches using QueryDSL and Blaze-Persistence.
Generate sales reporting aggregated by category and store.
Expose actuator endpoints for health checks and Prometheus metrics.
project_overview.architecture: A layered architecture consisting of Spring REST Controllers, business service components, Spring Data JPA / Querydsl repositories, and entity models mapped to the Sakila database schema. Cross-cutting concerns are handled via servlet filters, global exception handlers, and security filter chains.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Security and Authentication

cross_cutting_concerns.description: Centralized handling of application exceptions mapped to standardized error response formats.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Caching
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Redis-backed caching configuration utilizing Lettuce connection pooling.

domains.name: application
domains.summary: The application domain consists of the main entry point class that bootstraps the Spring Boot application context. It initializes the overall Spring REST service without defining any domain-specific logic or REST endpoints within this class. There are no additional classes or cross-class inconsistencies present in this functional area.
key_responsibilities: Bootstraps the Spring Boot application context

domains.name: auth
domains.summary: The auth domain provides user authentication, authorization, and credential management services using Spring Security and JWT tokens. It maps user roles to database storage via custom JPA converters and entities linked to repository layers. The LoginController exposes a single endpoint for user login, delegating authentication and token generation to security and user detail services. Data transfer objects and value objects support role definitions and credential transfer throughout the authentication lifecycle.
key_responsibilities: Authenticate users via Spring Security AuthenticationManager and custom user details services
Generate JWT tokens for successfully authenticated login requests
Persist and manage authority entities and credentials using Spring Data JPA
Map between EnumSet of UserRole and database strings using custom attribute converters
Load user details by username or email for security validation

domains.name: catalog
domains.summary: The catalog domain provides Spring REST endpoints for managing and querying actors, films, and their relationships using HATEOAS representation models, QueryDSL, and Blaze-Persistence. It coordinates business logic through transactional services while utilizing custom JPA attribute converters and MapStruct mappers for data transformation. Cross-class analysis reveals minor inconsistencies including misleading exception messages on entity lookups and redundant repository annotations. Overall, the layer separates persistence entities, DTOs, and resource assemblers cleanly.
key_responsibilities: Expose REST endpoints for CRUD operations and relationship management on actors and films
Transform domain entities and DTOs into HATEOAS-compliant response models
Execute custom pagination, filtering, and text searches using QueryDSL and Blaze-Persistence
Map database records to application enums and types using custom JPA attribute converters
Enforce transactional boundaries and caching policies in service implementations

domains.name: common
domains.summary: The common domain provides foundational building blocks, including shared constants, enumerations, DTOs, entity definitions, mapping contracts, and utilities. It implements security features such as JWT-based authentication filters, providers, tokens, and token providers for request authorization. Additionally, it handles cross-cutting concerns like servlet-based MDC request logging, custom Jackson serialization, and global exception management.
key_responsibilities: Define domain-wide enumerations and string constants for categories, countries, languages, ratings, and features
Provide reusable DTO interfaces, error response structures, and name value objects
Support object mapping via generic mapper interfaces and custom MapStruct qualifiers
Implement JWT-based security filters, authentication providers, and token generation utilities
Populate and clear SLF4J MDC contexts for incoming HTTP requests via a servlet filter
Handle application exceptions globally and map them to standardized error responses
Provide utility methods for constructing dynamic Querydsl boolean expressions

domains.name: config
domains.summary: The config domain centralizes application infrastructure setup, including security, persistence, caching, and request tracing. It provides beans for password encoding, authentication management, and stateless security filter chains alongside authorization rules. Persistence configuration initializes JPA repositories, QueryDSL factories, and Blaze-Persistence components, while Redis configuration establishes connection factories, templates, and short-lived caching policies. Additionally, request logging and tracing filters are explicitly registered to support HTTP telemetry.
key_responsibilities: Configure authentication manager and password encoding beans
Define stateless security filter chains and URL authorization rules
Enable JPA repositories across multiple service base packages
Expose QueryDSL and Blaze-Persistence query factories
Configure Lettuce Redis connection factory and caching serialization
Register request logging and MDC tracing filters

domains.name: customer
domains.summary: The customer domain provides REST APIs for managing customer profiles, retrieving customer details, and querying associated payment and rental records. It employs Spring MVC controllers, HATEOAS representation assemblers, services, and a Querydsl-backed repository layer for complex filtering. Transformations between entities and DTOs are handled via MapStruct, while access control protects mutating endpoints.

It integrates Spring REST controllers with HATEOAS assemblers, services, Spring Data JPA repositories, and MapStruct mappers to handle CRUD operations and pagination. Custom repository implementations are partially stubbed, and various entity attributes rely on custom JPA attribute converters for enums and geometry types.

It exposes a secured REST API supporting paginated retrieval, detailed views, updates, and deletion of payment resources. Spring Data JPA with QueryDSL powers the data access layer, while MapStruct handles object mapping and Spring HATEOAS formats representation models.

domains.summary: The rental domain manages DVD rentals, returns, and associated records using a layered architecture comprising REST controllers, services, repositories, and MapStruct mappers. It exposes secure endpoints under /api/v1/rentals protected by ROLE_MANAGE security, supporting operations such as pagination, creation, updates, and custom queries via Querydsl. Entities map directly to the sakila.rental database table, establishing relationships with inventory, customers, and staff. HATEOAS assemblers decorate responses with self and collection links for improved navigability.

domains.summary: The store domain manages physical store locations, staff assignments, inventory stock levels, and aggregated sales reporting by category and store. findings.title: Throws IllegalArgumentException on null attribute
